record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.original_question: How can one construct and use, in a practical way, a formalism for Euclidean random matrices in which the supersymmetry of the problem plays a crucial role?

evidence.quote: In the framework of Euclidean random theory there are two questions that are quite relevant and may be the most interesting for Euclidean Random theory: • How to construct and to use in a practical way a formalism where the supersymmetry of the problem plays a crucial role?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}$ be points drawn independently and uniformly at random from a region $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of density $\rho=N/|\Omega|$. A Euclidean random matrix is an $N\times N$ random matrix $M$ whose entries have the form $M_{ij}=f(x_i,x_j)$ (or a related form such as $M_{ij}=\delta_{ij}\sum_k f(x_i,x_k)-f(x_i,x_j)$) for some fixed deterministic function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$. One is interested in the ensemble-averaged resolvent and spectral density of $M$, as well as in averages of products of resolvents (which control level correlations).

Recall that the supersymmetry method of Efetov–Wegner expresses such ensemble averages by introducing pairs of commuting and anticommuting (Grassmann) auxiliary variables, rewriting $\langle\det(z-M)^{-1}\rangle$ and $\langle\det(z_+ - M)^{-1}\det(z_- - M)\rangle$ as Gaussian integrals over a supervector, and then performing the disorder average to obtain an effective action invariant under a graded (super)group. For standard (Wigner / invariant) random matrix ensembles this leads to a nonlinear $\sigma$-model on a supermanifold and yields exact results for spectral statistics.

Problem: For the Euclidean random matrix ensembles described above, develop an explicit and practically usable supersymmetric formalism. Concretely:

(a) Write down a representation of $\langle\det(z-M)^{-1}\rangle$ and $\langle\det(z_+-M)^{-1}\det(z_--M)\rangle$ as integrals over commuting and Grassmann fields indexed by the positions $\{x_i\}$, and carry out the average over the point positions to obtain an effective action $S[\Psi,\bar\Psi]$ depending only on bilinears in the supervector field.

(b) Identify the relevant graded symmetry group of this effective action and the corresponding Goldstone/saddle manifold that controls the low-energy spectral physics.

(c) Use this formalism to derive, in a controlled approximation (e.g.\ high density $\rho\to\infty$, or a chosen $1/N$ expansion), closed expressions for the averaged density of states and the two-point spectral correlation function.

Does there exist such a supersymmetric construction for Euclidean random matrices that is computationally tractable and reproduces known limits?
artifact.status_search_result: While the supersymmetry method is well-developed for standard random matrix ensembles (Efetov, Verbaarschot, Zirnbauer) and for random band matrices, a fully practical supersymmetric formalism specifically tailored to Euclidean random matrices—where randomness enters through the positions of points rather than directly through matrix entries—does not appear to have been established as a standard tool. Searches return general references on supersymmetry in RMT and on Euclidean random matrices separately, but no work claiming a complete practical supersymmetric reformulation of the Euclidean random matrix problem. The question is therefore best regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: The Supersymmetric Method in Random Matrix Theory and Applications to QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Review of the supersymmetric method in standard random matrix ensembles; does not provide a practical formalism for Euclidean random matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Supersymmetry is well developed for standard RMT but not specifically for Euclidean random matrices.

status_evidence.title: SUSY Statistical Mechanics and Random Band Matrices (Spencer)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes applying SUSY to random band matrices, not to Euclidean random matrices defined through random point configurations.
status_evidence.claim: Existing practical SUSY formalisms address band/invariant ensembles, leaving the Euclidean case unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean random matrices and their applications in physics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of methods used for Euclidean random matrices; supersymmetry is not presented as a standard practical technique.
status_evidence.claim: Reviews of ERM methodology do not contain a worked-out practical supersymmetric formalism.
